quickSummary: Both dicot and monocot roots have epiblema without cuticle, exarch xylem (centripetal), and radial bundles. Dicot roots have 2-6 xylem bundles (diarch to hexarch), polygonal vessels, an inconspicuous pith, and undergo secondary growth. Monocot roots have >6 xylem bundles (polyarch: 12-20), circular vessels, a large parenchymatous pith, and lack secondary growth.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Comparative Root Anatomy Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Comparative Root Anatomy Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Anatomical Parameter | Dicot Root (e.g., *Helianthus* - Sunflower) | Monocot Root (e.g., *Zea mays* - Maize) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epiblema / Rhizodermis** | Single-layered; lacks cuticle; bears unicellular root hairs | Single-layered; lacks cuticle; bears unicellular root hairs |
| **Cortex** | Broad, homogeneous parenchymatous tissue with intercellular spaces | Broad, homogeneous parenchymatous tissue; outer layers form **Exodermis** in older roots |
| **Endodermis** | Distinct; cells feature suberized **Casparian Strips**; **Passage Cells** present opposite protoxylem | Distinct; Casparian strips present; becomes heavily suberized (thick O-shaped walls) in older roots |
| **Pericycle** | Single-layered; gives rise to **lateral roots AND part of the vascular cambium** | Single-layered; gives rise **ONLY to lateral roots** (No cambium formation) |
| **Vascular Bundle Number** | **Diarch to Hexarch** ($2\text{--}6$ alternate xylem/phloem bundles) | **Polyarch** ($>6$, often $12\text{--}20$ alternate bundles) |
| **Protoxylem Condition** | **Exarch** (Protoxylem peripheral, Metaxylem central) | **Exarch** (Protoxylem peripheral, Metaxylem central) |
| **Xylem Vessel Shape** | Polygonal / Angular in cross-section | Oval / Circular in cross-section |
| **Pith (Medulla)** | Small, inconspicuous, or completely **ABSENT** | Large, well-developed, parenchymatous pith |
| **Secondary Growth** | **PRESENT** (Vascular cambium and phellogen develop later) | **ABSENT** entirely |
